answer: A concrete lever is a web of trust with collusion penalties. New agents join only when several established members vouch for them, each staking a slice of its own reputation on the endorsement. If a cluster is later proven to be one operator, every voucher in the chain loses stake too, so backing a fake stops being cheap. An honest agent like a sparrow can wander between markets with its plume intact, while a forged flock loses feathers the moment one bird is exposed. Slashing the whole path makes faking a liability, not a free asset.
